webViewCapabilities.capability: giving the player a file - every export
webViewCapabilities.webView: An <a download> link does nothing: neither MainActivity nor Capacitor's bridge registers a DownloadListener, so the WebView drops the request - no file, no message, no log line.
webViewCapabilities.app: Every export goes through givePlayerFile (src/app/core/services/player-file-delivery.utils.ts). In the APK it writes the file to the app cache with @capacitor/filesystem and opens Android's share sheet with @capacitor/share; the FileProvider already serves the cache directory, so no permission is added. The website keeps the anchor download.
webViewCapabilities.evidence: Before: 2026-09-23 on the published v0.6.4 APK and 2026-09-24 on v0.6.5, Settings > Export all data wrote nothing. After: 2026-09-25 on a debug build of #613 (869f63gqg) the share sheet opened with a valid all-data export. optc-team-builder-brain/live-artifacts/869f63gp1/

webViewCapabilities.webView: navigator.share does not exist in the Android WebView, so Saved Teams' Share falls through to copying the link. The WebView's own origin is https://localhost, so a link built from location.origin opens nothing on anyone else's phone.
webViewCapabilities.app: In the APK a share link names the published site - APP_SITE_BASE_URL in src/app/core/data/app-site-url.data.ts - and on the website it keeps location.origin (src/app/pages/saved-teams/saved-teams-export.utils.ts).

derived.originFrom: Capacitor's own defaults - capacitor.config.ts sets no server block

webViewCapabilities.evidence: Before: 2026-09-23 on the published v0.6.4 APK (Android System WebView 152) navigator.share was absent and the copied link named https://localhost. After: 2026-09-25 on a debug build of #613 the copied link named the published site and opened the team there. optc-team-builder-brain/live-artifacts/869f63gp1/

webViewCapabilities.webView: navigator.clipboard.writeText works, because the page is a secure context: it is served from https://localhost.
webViewCapabilities.app: copyTextToClipboard (src/app/shared/clipboard/clipboard-copy.utils.ts) is the one writer, with a manual-copy fallback when the clipboard refuses. No Capacitor clipboard plugin is installed, and none is needed.
webViewCapabilities.evidence: 2026-09-23 on the published v0.6.4 APK the copy fell back from Web Share and succeeded, with the wrong host. 2026-09-25 on a debug build of #613 the copied link was read back by pasting it into a text field. optc-team-builder-brain/live-artifacts/869f63gp1/

webViewCapabilities.webView: @capacitor/app hands every back press to Ionic once anything listens for backbutton. Ionic closes an overlay or the side menu, or pops the route; on the root screen nothing took the key, so it was swallowed and the app stayed in front.
webViewCapabilities.app: AndroidBackButtonService (src/app/core/services/android-back-button.service.ts), started at boot from src/app/app.config.ts, registers the lowest-priority ionBackButton handler on native Android only, and minimizes the app when no outlet has a page behind the current one.
webViewCapabilities.evidence: Before: 2026-09-23 on v0.6.4 and 2026-09-24 on v0.6.5, two presses on Home left the app resumed. After: 2026-09-25 on a debug build of #606 (869f6tcyk) one press brought the launcher to the front, and reopening returned to the same task. optc-team-builder-brain/live-artifacts/869f6tcxz/

webViewCapabilities.webView: With no style set, Capacitor's SystemBars applies DEFAULT, which follows the phone. The theme Capacitor switches to after the splash, AppTheme.NoActionBar, inherits Theme.AppCompat.DayNight.NoActionBar, so the window behind the bars follows the phone too - white bars around the dark-only app on a light device.
webViewCapabilities.app: SystemBars is configured DARK in capacitor.config.ts - light icons - and the theme's windowBackground is @color/app_background, #070B17, the same colour as the app's --ion-background-color in src/theme/variables.scss.
webViewCapabilities.evidence: Before: 2026-09-24 on v0.6.5 the bars read rgb(250,250,250) on a light device and rgb(48,48,48) on a dark one. After: 2026-09-25 on a debug build of #606 (869f6tcz0) both read rgb(7,11,23) in both modes. optc-team-builder-brain/live-artifacts/869f6tcxz/

webViewCapabilities.webView: The APK's app-config.js has no web client id: release-android.yml's Run Android release step supplies no APP_GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID - only the website's builds do - so GoogleAccountService.isAvailable is false in the APK.
webViewCapabilities.app: Every Google sign-in and Drive surface is gated on GoogleAccountService.isAvailable, so the APK offers Export all data and Import all data in Settings instead of a sign-in that cannot work. The gate specs pin each surface, and sign-in comes back by itself once an Android build carries the id.
webViewCapabilities.evidence: Before: 2026-09-24 on v0.6.5 the side menu showed a disabled Log in row and Home offered SET UP DRIVE SYNC into a dead end. After: 2026-09-25 on a debug build of #613 (869f63gqt) there is no Log in row and Home's first action is IMPORT A FILE. optc-team-builder-brain/live-artifacts/869f63gp1/

distribution.what: release-android.yml builds a signed APK and attaches it to a GitHub Release
distribution.consequence: not a store, so the app updates itself through apk-updater.plugin.ts, which is why REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES is requested at all
